severity_notes:
- An acked `Durable` record that is not on disk, or does not replay after a crash, is severe. So is anything that lets two daemons own one `wab_dir`.
- A change to the on-disk WAB format, the wire protocol or a published crate's public API without a version decision is severe: it needs the owner (semver, the `docs_drift` guards).
- A panic reachable from a client frame, a stored segment or a config value is critical.
- A secret (sink URL credentials, bearer token, crates.io token) reaching a log, a `Debug` string, argv or `/status` is critical.
- Anything that loosens a security default (peer UID check, socket permissions, mTLS on TCP) is severe, and is never fixed overnight without the owner.

Scope of this epic (from its spec, docs/superpowers/temper/cleanup-2026-11/spec.md): the whole repository at the branch tip, NOT only `git diff main...epic/cleanup-2026-11` (the branch starts equal to main, so that diff is just the spec). Review the code itself, in your lens's area (the spec's Scope table). A finding needs an input and a wrong result that a verifier can reproduce; style, refactors and perf ideas are not findings.
These are owner items (kind owner), never fixes: a change to the WAB or `.confirmed` format, the wire protocol, `--json` shapes or a published crate's public API; loosening a security default; a new or upgraded dependency; D10 (explicit missing --config only WARNs: a deferred owner decision).
build_rule:
Every build, test, clippy or gate on beast runs as a jobq job: never run cargo, a gate script or a test binary directly in your ssh session (beast's ~/agents/CLAUDE.md; a session that compiled outside jobq was OOM-killed). Work in a worktree under ~/work/weir/ on beast; jobq's --cwd is that worktree's physical path (`pwd -P`).

Submit, then wait in the foreground (a single Bash call must stay under 10 minutes, so never use `jobq run` for a gate, and never end your turn while a job of yours is queued or running):
  ssh beast 'cd <worktree> && JOBQ_SUBMITTER=temper-cleanup ~/.local/bin/jobq submit --profile rust --project weir --cores 4 --mem 4G --timeout 3h --cwd "$(pwd -P)" --name <your-label>-quick -- bash .temper/gate-quick.sh'
  ssh beast '~/.local/bin/jobq wait <id>'   (call it again, with a Bash timeout of 600000 ms, until the job ends; its exit status is the gate's)
The full gate is the same with `--mem 8G --timeout 5h --name <your-label>-full -- bash .temper/gate-full.sh`. One cargo command (a reproduction, a single test) is the same with `--mem 4G --timeout 1h --name <your-label>-run -- bash .temper/gate-run.sh <cargo args>`, e.g. `... -- bash .temper/gate-run.sh test -p weir-wab segment`.
A job's env is cleared: pass variables as `-- env VAR=value bash .temper/gate-run.sh ...`. Read results from `~/.local/bin/jobq logs <id> --tail 400` (it prints only the last 200 lines by default) and from the gate's summary, /srv/bulk/Projects/weir/logs/gate/<worktree dir name>/latest-<quick|full|run>/summary.txt, whose last line is `GATE <name> rc=N`. A job's peak memory includes page cache: if a job is OOM-killed, resubmit once with a 2G larger --mem and say so in your result. Never cancel or touch another submitter's jobs. Keep at most one job of yours queued or running at a time. Beast's rule is at most 4 builds of this run at once: before each submit, run `ssh beast 'JOBQ_SUBMITTER=temper-cleanup ~/.local/bin/jobq list --mine | grep -cE " (queued|running) "'`; while it prints 4 or more, wait with `ssh beast 'sleep 120'` and check again.
Never set CARGO_TARGET_DIR or make another target dir: the gate slots are the build dirs; a gate that waits for a slot or for jobq's memory is normal. Never run sudo, never run the chaos harness's power-cut campaign, never touch docker images, volumes or containers that aren't weir's, never write the CI-skip token in a commit message. Commits carry only the `Temper-Task` trailer: no Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session or "Generated with" lines. Never print a secret or token.
A fix also adds one line under CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased]` (replace its "Nothing yet." line), in `### Fixed`, or `### Changed` for a behaviour an operator can notice, in the file's existing style. The `docs_drift` and `demo_drift` tests guard figures and version strings in the docs: if a fix trips one, fix the doc, never weaken the guard.
Clean up what you start on beast (test processes, tmux servers); leave worktrees in place.

selected.summary: HTTP sink URL is logged through redact_url_password, which only scrubs userinfo and a 10-key query denylist, so secrets in the path or in other query keys reach the startup INFO line and, through reqwest's error Display (" for url ({url})", reqwest-0.12.28 error.rs:268), every transport-error retry (sink/http.rs:256) and the HEAD-probe Down reason (http.rs:653).
selected.input: sink_type="http" with sink_url = "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T0/B0/SECRETTOKEN" or a presigned URL "https://b.s3.amazonaws.com/k?X-Amz-Signature=abc&X-Amz-Security-Token=xyz" (or ?client_secret=, ?key=, ?code=), then any connect failure to the sink
selected.wrong_result: The INFO line "sink: http" prints url=https://hooks.slack.com/services/T0/B0/SECRETTOKEN (or the X-Amz-Signature / X-Amz-Security-Token values) verbatim, and the same full URL is in HttpSinkError::Transport, which the drain re-logs on every retry and stores in the admin status text. The keys are matched exactly and case-insensitively against password/passwd/pwd/token/access_token/secret/api_key/apikey/sig/signature, so X-Amz-Signature, client_secret and similar keys pass through. config_view.rs:35 already says path secrets are not covered by these redactors. Also confirmed by status-metrics-and-admin-r3-01: sanitize_admin_text passes the same URL into the admin /status sink-failure text.

selected.summary: After fix:sinks-r3-05 (05b1d00) the Postgres sink strands SQLSTATE 25006 read_only_sql_transaction, but the configuration reference's Postgres error-classification table and the postgres.rs module doc still say it is permanent and dead-letters the batch.
selected.input: Read docs/operations/configuration.md lines 2114-2122 and crates/weir-server/src/sink/postgres.rs lines 93-107 on the branch tip, against postgres.rs:507 (`|| state == &SqlState::READ_ONLY_SQL_TRANSACTION`) and its CHANGELOG entry.
selected.wrong_result: The table lists only 40P01, 55P03, 57014 and 57P01/57P02/57P03 as transient, then `| anything else | permanent | dead-letter the batch |`; `git grep -n 25006` finds it only in CHANGELOG.md and postgres.rs. An operator is told a read-only or hot-standby target dead-letters the batch, while the code strands and retries it. Fix: add a 25006 read_only_sql_transaction row (transient, retry) to the table and a matching line to the module doc. Found by the regression check on fix:sinks-r3-05.
